metadata.title: Equivalence of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$-actions on handlebodies of genus $g$

extraction_notes.note: The main proof is headed 'Proof of Theorem 2.2', but no Theorem 2.2 exists (2.2 is the realizability lemma); it proves the main Theorem 1.1, so its proves edge goes to TP2.
The proof of Proposition 2.5 says 'By Lemma 2.2, this is impossible', but the argument is the content of Lemma 2.3; kept the stated edge from LP1 (0.9) and added LP2 -> PP3 at 0.6.

A forced line break written as '\\$\prod' in the proof of Lemma 2.4 makes the step checker's math parser misread the rest of the body as math; the per-property steps after it could not be separated, so properties (4),(2),(3),(6),(7),(1) form one step.

PrP1 and LP1 have no proof (only 'similar proof technique / adaptation from [KM]') and the corollaries are asserted to follow directly from Theorem 1.1 without argument; given rigor semi_formal and origin paper.
Unproved 'Note that' assertions about quotients and the orbifold fundamental group kept as claims; ClP3 marked external standard fact rather than a paper contribution.

Figure 1 (the tikz graph of groups) carries the definition of Γ(v); only the prose sentence referring to it is extracted (DP4). The sentence on canonical form/normalized conditions from [KM] was left out as a bare pointer.

FR.text: D. I. Fuchs-Rabinovitch, \emph{On the automorphism group of free products}, I, Mat. Sb. 8 (1940), 265-276. \smallskip

KM.text: J. Kalliongis and A. Miller, \emph{Equivalence and strong equivalence of actions on handlebodies}, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 308 (1988). \smallskip

JK.text: J. Kim, \emph{Structures of geometric quotient orbifolds of three-dimensional $g$-manifolds of genus 2}, J. Korean Math. Soc. 46 (2009), No. 4, pp. 859-893. \smallskip

MMZ.text: D. McCullough, A. Miller, and B. Zimmerman, \emph{Group actions on handlebodies}, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 59 (1989) 373-416. \smallskip

JPL.text: J. Prince-Lubawy, \emph{Equivalence of cyclic $p^2$-actions on handlebodies}. (In preparation) \smallskip

nodes.name: G-action on a handlebody
nodes.statement: A {$\mathbf{G}$-action} on  a handlebody $V_g$, of genus $g>0$, is a group monomorphism $\phi:{\mathbf{G}}\longrightarrow{}$Homeo$^+(V_g)$, where Homeo$^+(V_g)$ denotes the group of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of $V_g$.
nodes.statement_short: A G-action on V_g is a monomorphism from G into the orientation-preserving homeomorphism group of V_g.

nodes.name: Equivalence of actions
nodes.statement: Two actions $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ on $V_g$ are said to be equivalent if and only if there exists an orientation-preserving homeomorphism $h$ of $V_g$ such that $\phi_2(x)=h\circ\phi_1(x)\circ{h^{-1}}$ for all $x\in\mathbf{G}$.
nodes.statement_short: Two actions are equivalent if conjugate by an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of V_g.

nodes.name: Finite group actions on handlebodies correspond to graphs of groups
nodes.statement: From \cite{MMZ}, the action of any finite group $\mathbf{G}$ on $V_g$ corresponds to a collection of graphs of groups.
assumptions: the action of any finite group $\mathbf{G}$ on $V_g$
conclusions: corresponds to a collection of graphs of groups

nodes.name: 5-tuple v
nodes.statement: Let v\ $=(r,s,t,m,n)$ be an ordered $5$-tuple of nonnegative integers.

nodes.name: Graph of groups (Γ(v),G(v)) and handlebody orbifold V(Γ(v),G(v))
nodes.statement: The graph of groups $(\Gamma($v$),\mathbf{G(v)})$ in canonical form, shown in Figure 1, determines a handlebody orbifold $V(\Gamma($v$),\mathbf{G(v)})$. The orbifold $V(\Gamma($v$),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$ is constructed in a similar manner as described in \cite{KM}.
nodes.statement_short: The canonical graph of groups of Figure 1 (parameters v) determines the handlebody orbifold V(Γ(v),G(v)), built as in Kalliongis-Miller.

nodes.name: Every Z4-quotient is of type V(Γ(v),G(v))
nodes.statement: Note that the quotient of any $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$-action on $V_g$ is an orbifold of this type, up to homeomorphism.
conclusions: is an orbifold of this type, up to homeomorphism

nodes.name: Unique Z4-action on genus 2 handlebody
nodes.statement: As we will see, there is exactly one equivalence class of $Z_4$-actions on the handlebody of genus 2.
conclusions: there is exactly one equivalence class of $Z_4$-actions

nodes.name: Main theorem: classification of Z4-actions on handlebodies
nodes.statement: If $\mathbb{Z}_4$ acts on $V_g$, where $g>0$, then $V_g/\mathbb{Z}_4$ is homeomorphic to $V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$ for some 5-tuple ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ of nonnegative integers with $r+s+t+m+n>0$ and $g+3=4(r+s+m)+3t+2n$. The number of equivalence classes of $\mathbb{Z}_4$-actions on $V_g$ with this quotient type is $m$ if $r+s+t=0$, and $m+1$ if $r+s+t>0$.
conclusions: $V_g/\mathbb{Z}_4$ is homeomorphic to $V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$ for some 5-tuple ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ of nonnegative integers with $r+s+t+m+n>0$ and $g+3=4(r+s+m)+3t+2n$
The number of equivalence classes of $\mathbb{Z}_4$-actions on $V_g$ with this quotient type is $m$ if $r+s+t=0$, and $m+1$ if $r+s+t>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Z4-quotients of V_g are the orbifolds V(Γ(v),G(v)) with g+3=4(r+s+m)+3t+2n; each type carries m classes if r+s+t=0 and m+1 otherwise.

nodes.name: Z4-actions on genus 3 handlebody
nodes.statement: To illustrate the theorem, let $g=3$. Then the genus equation becomes $6=4(r+s+m)+3t+2n$ so that $r+s+m$ must equal 0 or 1, and $(r,s,t,m,n)$ is one of $(0,0,2,0,0)$, $(1,0,0,0,1)$, $(0,1,0,0,1)$, or $(0,0,0,1,1)$. Applying Theorem 1.1 to these four possibilities shows that there are a total of $1+1+1+1=4$ equivalence classes of orientation-preserving $\mathbb{Z}_4$-actions on $V_3$.
nodes.statement_short: For g=3 the genus equation allows four 5-tuples, each giving one class, so 4 equivalence classes in total.

nodes.name: Even genus Z4-actions have fixed points
nodes.statement: Every $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action on a handlebody of even genus must have an interval of fixed points and at least two fixed points on the boundary of the handlebody.
assumptions: Every $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action on a handlebody of even genus
conclusions: must have an interval of fixed points and at least two fixed points on the boundary of the handlebody

nodes.name: Z4-actions free on the boundary
nodes.statement: Every $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action that is free on the boundary of the handlebody will have $t=n=0$ and $g\equiv1$(mod 4).
assumptions: Every $\mathbb{Z}_4$-action that is free on the boundary of the handlebody

nodes.name: Orbifold fundamental group is an extension
nodes.statement: The orbifold fundamental group of $V(\Gamma($v$), {\mathbf{G(v)}})$ is an extension of $\pi_1(V_g)$ by the group $\mathbf{G}$.
conclusions: The orbifold fundamental group of $V(\Gamma($v$), {\mathbf{G(v)}})$ is an extension of $\pi_1(V_g)$ by the group $\mathbf{G}$.

nodes.name: Free product decomposition of the orbifold fundamental group
nodes.statement: We may view the fundamental group  as a free product $G_1*G_2*G_3*\cdots*{G_{r+s+t+m+n}}$, where $G_i$ is isomorphic to either $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}_{4}\times\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$, $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}$, or $\mathbb{Z}_2$.
nodes.statement_short: The orbifold fundamental group is a free product of r+s+t+m+n factors G_i, each Z, Z4×Z, Z4, Z2×Z or Z2.

nodes.name: Generators of the orbifold fundamental group
nodes.statement: We establish notation similar to \cite{KM} and denote the generators of the orbifold fundamental group by $\{a_i: 1\leq{i}\leq{r}\}\cup\{b_j,c_j:1\leq{j}\leq{s}\}\cup\{d_k:1\leq{k}\leq{t}\}\cup\{e_l,f_l:1\leq{l}\leq{m}\}\cup\{g_q:1\leq{q}\leq{n}\}$ such that $b_j^{4}=d_k^{4}=1$, $[b_j,c_j]=1$, $e_l^2=g_q^2=1$, and $[e_l,f_l]=1$.
nodes.definiendum: $a_i, b_j, c_j, d_k, e_l, f_l, g_q$
nodes.statement_short: Names the generators a_i, b_j, c_j, d_k, e_l, f_l, g_q of the orbifold fundamental group with their torsion and commuting relations.

nodes.name: Pairs ((Γ(v),G(v)),λ)
nodes.statement: Consider the set of pairs $((\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda)$, where $\lambda$ is a finite injective epimorphism from $\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ onto $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$.

nodes.name: Finite injective epimorphism
nodes.statement: We say $\lambda$ is finite injective since the kernel of $\lambda$ is a free group of rank $g$.
differentia: the kernel of $\lambda$ is a free group of rank $g$

nodes.name: Kernel is the image of an orbifold covering
nodes.statement: We consider only finite injective epimorphisms such that ker($\lambda$)$=$im($\nu_*$) for some orbifold covering $\nu:V\longrightarrow V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$.

nodes.name: Covering handlebody genus formula
nodes.statement: Since $V$ is a handlebody with torsion free fundamental group, $V$ is homeomorphic to a handlebody $V_g$ of genus $g=1-4\chi(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$.
assumptions: $V$ is a handlebody with torsion free fundamental group
conclusions: $V$ is homeomorphic to a handlebody $V_g$ of genus $g=1-4\chi(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$

nodes.name: Equivalence of pairs
nodes.statement: Define an equivalence relation on this set of pairs by setting $((\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda)\equiv(({\Gamma}({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda')$ if and only if there exists an orbifold homeomorphism $h:V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})\longrightarrow{V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})}$ such that $\lambda'=\lambda\circ{h_*}$.
nodes.statement_short: Two pairs are equivalent when λ' = λ∘h_* for an orbifold homeomorphism h of V(Γ(v),G(v)).

nodes.name: Delta set Δ(Z4,V_g,V(Γ(v),G(v)))
nodes.statement: We define the set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set of equivalence classes $[((\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda)]$ under this relation.

nodes.name: Set E of equivalence classes of Z4-actions
nodes.statement: Denote the  set set of equivalence classes $\mathscr{E}(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set  $\{[\phi]\ |\ \phi:\mathbb{Z}_{4}\longrightarrow{Homeo^+(V_g)}\ and\ V_g/\phi\simeq{V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})}\}$.
nodes.statement_short: E is the set of equivalence classes of Z4-actions on V_g whose quotient is V(Γ(v),G(v)).

nodes.name: Every Z4-action lies in some E set
nodes.statement: Note that given any $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$-action $\phi:\mathbb{Z}_{4}\longrightarrow{Homeo^+(V_g)}$, it must be the case that for some $V(\Gamma($v$),{\mathbf{G(v)}})$, $[\phi]\in\mathscr{E}(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$.

nodes.name: Correspondence between E and Δ
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$. The set $\mathscr{E}(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}))$ is in one-to-one correspondence with the set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ for every $g>0$.
conclusions: The set $\mathscr{E}(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}))$ is in one-to-one correspondence with the set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$
nodes.statement_short: Equivalence classes of Z4-actions with quotient V(Γ(v)) biject with equivalence classes of finite injective epimorphisms (the Δ set).

nodes.name: Realizability of automorphisms
nodes.statement:
If $\alpha$ is an automorphism of $\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),\mathbf{G(v)}))$, then $\alpha$ is realizable $[\alpha=h_*$ for some orientation-preserving homeomorphism $h:V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})\longrightarrow{V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}})}]$ if and only if 
\begin{align}
\alpha(b_j)&=x_jb_{\sigma(j)}^{\varepsilon_j}x_j^{-1},\notag \\
\alpha(c_j)&=x_jb_{\sigma(j)}^{{v_j}}c_{\sigma(j)}^{\varepsilon_j}x_j^{-1},\notag \\
\alpha(d_k)&=y_kd_{\tau(k)}^{\delta_k}y_k^{-1},\notag \\
\alpha(e_l)&=u_le_{\gamma(l)}^{\varepsilon_l'}u_l^{-1},\notag \\
\alpha(f_l)&=u_le_{\gamma(l)}^{{w_l}}f_{\gamma(l)}^{\varepsilon_l'}u_l^{-1}, and\notag \\
\alpha(g_q)&=z_qg_{\xi(q)}^{\delta_q'}z_q^{-1},\notag
\end{align}
for some $x_j, y_k, u_l, z_q\in{\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),\mathbf{G(v)}))}$; $\sigma\in{\sum_s}$, $\tau\in{\sum_t}$, $\gamma\in{\sum_m}$, $\xi\in{\sum_n}$; $\varepsilon_j, \delta_k, \varepsilon_l', \delta_q'\in{\{+1,-1\}}$; and $0\leq{v_j}<4$, $0\leq{w_l}<2$.\\
Note that $\Sigma_l$ is the permutation group on l letters.
nodes.statement_short: An automorphism of the orbifold fundamental group is induced by an orientation-preserving homeomorphism iff it acts on b,c,d,e,f,g generators by conjugated, permuted, signed (and twisted) images.
nodes.label: real

nodes.name: Fuchs-Rabinovitch generating set for automorphisms of free products
nodes.statement: Note that from \cite{FR}, a generating set for the automorphisms of the orbifold fundamental group $\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$),\mathbf{G(v)}))$ is the set of mappings $\{\rho_{ji}(x), \lambda_{ji}(x), \mu_{ji}(x), \omega_{ij}, \sigma_i, \phi_i\}$ whose definitions may be found in \cite{FR}.
conclusions: a generating set for the automorphisms of the orbifold fundamental group $\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$),\mathbf{G(v)}))$ is the set of mappings $\{\rho_{ji}(x), \lambda_{ji}(x), \mu_{ji}(x), \omega_{ij}, \sigma_i, \phi_i\}$

nodes.name: First five Fuchs-Rabinovitch maps are realizable
nodes.statement: The first five maps are realizable.
conclusions: The first five maps are realizable.

nodes.name: Form of realizable φ_i
nodes.statement: The realizable $\phi_i$'s are of the form found in Lemma 2.2 and will be used in the remaining arguments of this paper.

nodes.name: Non-equivalence when f_j maps to a generator
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ with $m>0$ and let \\$\lambda_1,\lambda_2:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms such that there exists a $j$ with $\lambda_1(f_j)$ being a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ and $\lambda_2(f_i)$ is not a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for all $i$. Then $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ are not equivalent.
assumptions: $\lambda_1,\lambda_2:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms such that there exists a $j$ with $\lambda_1(f_j)$ being a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ and $\lambda_2(f_i)$ is not a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for all $i$
nodes.statement_short: If λ1 sends some f_j to a generator of Z4 and λ2 sends no f_i to a generator, then λ1 and λ2 are inequivalent.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda_1,\lambda_2:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms such that $\lambda_1$ sends $f_j$ to a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for some $j$ and $\lambda_2$ does not send $f_i$ to a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for all $i$. We may assume that ${\lambda_2}(f_i)=0$ for all $i$ by composing $\lambda_2$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $f_i$ to the element $e_i^{w_i}f_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $w_i=0$ if $\lambda_2(f_i)=0$ and $w_i=1$ if $\lambda_2(f_i)=2$. To show that $\lambda_1$ and ${\lambda_2}$ are not equivalent we will consider the element $f_j$ such that $\lambda_1(f_j)$ generates $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$. For contradiction, assume that $\lambda_1$ is equivalent to ${\lambda_2}$. Then by Lemma \ref{real}, there exists a realizable automorphism $\alpha$ such that $\alpha(f_j)=ue_m^wf_m^{\pm1}u^{-1}$, where $u\in{\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma(}$v${),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))}$ and $0\leq{w}<{2}$. Hence $\lambda_1(f_j)=w{\lambda_2}(e_m)$, where ${\lambda_2}(e_m)$ is a multiple of $2$, and hence $\lambda_1(f_j)$ is a multiple of $2$. This is impossible since $\lambda_1(f_j)$ is a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$. Therefore $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ cannot be equivalent, proving the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: normalize λ2(f_i)=0, then Lemma 2.2 forces λ1(f_j) to be a multiple of 2, not a generator.

nodes.name: Normal form of finite injective epimorphisms
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ and let $\lambda:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ be a finite injective epimorphism. There exists a finite injective epimorphism $\tilde{\lambda}:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ equivalent to $\lambda$ such that the following hold:
\begin{list}{(\arabic{qcounter})~}{\usecounter{qcounter}}
\item $\tilde{\lambda}(a_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(a_{r})=1$.
\item $\tilde{\lambda}(b_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(b_{s})=1$.
\item $\tilde{\lambda}(c_i)=0$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{s}$.
\item $\tilde{\lambda}(d_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(d_{t})=1$.
\item $\tilde{\lambda}(e_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(e_{m})={2}$.
\item $\tilde{\lambda}(f_i)=1$ for all $i\leq{k}$ some $0\leq{k}\leq{m}$.
\item $\tilde{\lambda}(f_i)=0$ for all $k<{i}\leq{m}$.
\item $\tilde{\lambda}(g_{1})=\cdots=\tilde{\lambda}(d_{n})=2$.
\end{list}
conclusions: There exists a finite injective epimorphism $\tilde{\lambda}:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ equivalent to $\lambda$ such that the following hold:
nodes.statement_short: Every finite injective epimorphism onto Z4 is equivalent to one with fixed normal-form values on all generators, with the first k f_i sent to 1 and the rest to 0.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ be a finite injective epimorphism. Properties (5) and (8) must occur since $\lambda$ is finite injective. Property (4) follows by composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism \\$\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $d_i$ to the element $d_i^{{\varepsilon}_i}$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $\varepsilon_i=1$ if $\lambda(d_i)=1$ and $\varepsilon_i=-1$ if $\lambda(d_i)=3$. Property (2) follows by a similar technique. Assuming property (2) holds, property (3) follows by composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $c_i$ to the element $b_i^{-\lambda(c_i)}c_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. To show properties (6) and (7) hold, we may compose $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi$ sends the generator $f_i$ to the element $e_i^{z_i}f_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $z_i=1$ if $\lambda(f_i)=2$, $z_i=2$ if $\lambda(f_i)=0$ or $\lambda(f_i)=1$, and $z_i=-1$ if $\lambda(f_i)=3$. Furthermore, composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphisms $\omega_{ij}$ we may interchange $f_i$ as needed so that the first $k$ generators map to 1 and the last $m-k$ generators map to 0. Finally, to prove property (1) we may assume that there exists an element $x\in G_j$ (where $G_j$ is either $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$, $\mathbb{Z}_4\times\mathbb{Z}$, or $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}$) such that $\lambda(x)=1$. Note that we may compose $\lambda$ with a realizable automorphism that sends $x$ to $x^{-1}$ if needed. Now compose $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\rho_{ji}(x^{-\lambda(a_i)+1})$. It may be shown that $(\lambda\circ\alpha)(a_i)=1$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_short: Construct the normal form property by property, composing λ with realizable automorphisms φ_i, ω_ij and ρ_ji.

nodes.name: Equivalence of normal forms iff k=k'
nodes.statement: Let ${\mathbf{v}}=(r,s,t,m,n)$ with $m>0$ and let \\$\lambda,\lambda':\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms that satisfy the conclusion of Lemma 2.4, where $\lambda(f_i)=1$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{k}$ and $\lambda'(f_i)=1$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{k'}$. Then $\lambda$ is equivalent to $\lambda'$ if and only if $k=k'$.
assumptions: $\lambda,\lambda':\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms that satisfy the conclusion of Lemma 2.4, where $\lambda(f_i)=1$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{k}$ and $\lambda'(f_i)=1$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{k'}$
conclusions: $\lambda$ is equivalent to $\lambda'$ if and only if $k=k'$
nodes.statement_short: Two normal-form epimorphisms are equivalent exactly when they send the same number k of f_i to 1.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.5
nodes.statement: For a contradiction, assume that $\lambda$ is equivalent to $\lambda'$ and $k\neq{k'}$. Without loss of generality we may assume that $k>k'$. Hence, $\lambda$ maps at least one more generator $f_i$ to 1 as does $\lambda'$. This would mean that there must exist a realizable automorphism $\alpha$ such that $(\lambda\circ\alpha)(f_{k'+1})=0$. By Lemma 2.2, this is impossible. Thus, $k=k'$. For the reverse implication suppose that $k=k'$. Then $\lambda=\lambda'$, proving the proposition.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: if k>k', a realizable automorphism would send some f to 0, impossible; the converse is immediate.

nodes.name: Proof of the main theorem
nodes.statement: Define $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set of equivalence classes $[(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda]$ such that $\lambda(f_i)=0$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{m}$. Define $\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set of equivalence classes $[(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda]$ such that $\lambda(f_i)=1$ for at least one $i$ such that $1\leq{i}\leq{m}$. By Lemma 2.3, the delta set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ is the disjoint union $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\dot{\bigcup}\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$. Hence, the order of the delta set is the sum of the orders of the two sets $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ and $\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$. Applying Lemma 2.4 and Proposition 2.5, $|\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))|=m$ and \\$|\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))|=1$. Hence by Proposition 2.1, the theorem follows.
nodes.statement_short: Split the Δ set by whether some f_i maps to 1, count each part using the normal form and Proposition 2.5, and transfer via Proposition 2.1.

nodes.name: Normalize λ2
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda_1,\lambda_2:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ be two finite injective epimorphisms such that $\lambda_1$ sends $f_j$ to a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for some $j$ and $\lambda_2$ does not send $f_i$ to a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$ for all $i$. We may assume that ${\lambda_2}(f_i)=0$ for all $i$ by composing $\lambda_2$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $f_i$ to the element $e_i^{w_i}f_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $w_i=0$ if $\lambda_2(f_i)=0$ and $w_i=1$ if $\lambda_2(f_i)=2$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce λ1, λ2 and normalize λ2(f_i)=0 by a realizable automorphism.

nodes.name: Assume equivalence
nodes.statement: To show that $\lambda_1$ and ${\lambda_2}$ are not equivalent we will consider the element $f_j$ such that $\lambda_1(f_j)$ generates $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$. For contradiction, assume that $\lambda_1$ is equivalent to ${\lambda_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Focus on f_j and assume λ1 equivalent to λ2.

nodes.name: Apply realizability lemma
nodes.statement: Then by Lemma \ref{real}, there exists a realizable automorphism $\alpha$ such that $\alpha(f_j)=ue_m^wf_m^{\pm1}u^{-1}$, where $u\in{\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma(}$v${),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))}$ and $0\leq{w}<{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.2 gives the form of the realizing automorphism on f_j.

nodes.name: Derive contradiction
nodes.statement: Hence $\lambda_1(f_j)=w{\lambda_2}(e_m)$, where ${\lambda_2}(e_m)$ is a multiple of $2$, and hence $\lambda_1(f_j)$ is a multiple of $2$. This is impossible since $\lambda_1(f_j)$ is a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_{4}$. Therefore $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ cannot be equivalent, proving the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: λ1(f_j) would be even, contradicting that it generates Z4.

nodes.name: Properties (5) and (8)
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda:\pi_1^{orb}(V(\Gamma($v$), {\mathbf{G(v)}}))\longrightarrow{\mathbb{Z}_{4}}$ be a finite injective epimorphism. Properties (5) and (8) must occur since $\lambda$ is finite injective.
nodes.statement_short: Properties (5),(8) are forced by finite injectivity.

nodes.name: Properties (4), (2), (3), (6), (7) and (1)
nodes.statement: Property (4) follows by composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism \\$\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $d_i$ to the element $d_i^{{\varepsilon}_i}$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $\varepsilon_i=1$ if $\lambda(d_i)=1$ and $\varepsilon_i=-1$ if $\lambda(d_i)=3$. Property (2) follows by a similar technique. Assuming property (2) holds, property (3) follows by composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi_i$ sends the generator $c_i$ to the element $b_i^{-\lambda(c_i)}c_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. To show properties (6) and (7) hold, we may compose $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\phi_i$, where $\phi$ sends the generator $f_i$ to the element $e_i^{z_i}f_i$ and leaves all other generators fixed. Note that $z_i=1$ if $\lambda(f_i)=2$, $z_i=2$ if $\lambda(f_i)=0$ or $\lambda(f_i)=1$, and $z_i=-1$ if $\lambda(f_i)=3$. Furthermore, composing $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphisms $\omega_{ij}$ we may interchange $f_i$ as needed so that the first $k$ generators map to 1 and the last $m-k$ generators map to 0. Finally, to prove property (1) we may assume that there exists an element $x\in G_j$ (where $G_j$ is either $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}_4$, $\mathbb{Z}_4\times\mathbb{Z}$, or $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}$) such that $\lambda(x)=1$. Note that we may compose $\lambda$ with a realizable automorphism that sends $x$ to $x^{-1}$ if needed. Now compose $\lambda$ with the realizable automorphism $\prod\rho_{ji}(x^{-\lambda(a_i)+1})$. It may be shown that $(\lambda\circ\alpha)(a_i)=1$ for all $i$.
nodes.statement_short: Compose λ with realizable automorphisms (sign changes, twists φ_i, permutations ω_ij, and ρ_ji) to obtain the remaining properties.

nodes.name: Assume equivalence with k>k'
nodes.statement: For a contradiction, assume that $\lambda$ is equivalent to $\lambda'$ and $k\neq{k'}$. Without loss of generality we may assume that $k>k'$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume equivalence with k≠k', WLOG k>k'.

nodes.name: Required realizable automorphism
nodes.statement: Hence, $\lambda$ maps at least one more generator $f_i$ to 1 as does $\lambda'$. This would mean that there must exist a realizable automorphism $\alpha$ such that $(\lambda\circ\alpha)(f_{k'+1})=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Then some realizable automorphism must send f_{k'+1} to 0 under λ.

nodes.name: Contradiction via Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: By Lemma 2.2, this is impossible. Thus, $k=k'$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.2 rules this out, so k=k'.

nodes.name: Reverse implication
nodes.statement: For the reverse implication suppose that $k=k'$. Then $\lambda=\lambda'$, proving the proposition.
nodes.statement_short: If k=k' the normal forms coincide.

nodes.name: Split Δ into Δ0 and Δ1
nodes.statement: Define $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set of equivalence classes $[(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda]$ such that $\lambda(f_i)=0$ for all $1\leq{i}\leq{m}$. Define $\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ to be the set of equivalence classes $[(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}),\lambda]$ such that $\lambda(f_i)=1$ for at least one $i$ such that $1\leq{i}\leq{m}$. By Lemma 2.3, the delta set $\Delta(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ is the disjoint union $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))\dot{\bigcup}\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$. Hence, the order of the delta set is the sum of the orders of the two sets $\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$ and $\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Define Δ0, Δ1 by whether some f_i maps to 1; Lemma 2.3 makes Δ the disjoint union of Δ0 and Δ1, so the orders add.

nodes.name: Count Δ0 and Δ1
nodes.statement: Applying Lemma 2.4 and Proposition 2.5, $|\Delta_1(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))|=m$ and \\$|\Delta_0(\mathbb{Z}_{4},V_g,V(\Gamma({\mathbf{v}}),{\mathbf{G(v)}}))|=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Normal form and Proposition 2.5 give |Δ1|=m and |Δ0|=1.

nodes.name: Transfer to actions
nodes.statement: Hence by Proposition 2.1, the theorem follows.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 2.1 transfers the count to equivalence classes of actions.
